subject: Follow-up: workload profile & batching / concurrency assumptions
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: workload profile & batching / concurrency assumptions

Hi Emily — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + a couple of clarifying items so we can size a POC and cost simulation.

Recap from our convo:
- Two primary product workloads: 1) customer-facing chat assistant (sessioned, long history reuse), 2) background summarization & analytics (batch jobs, short-lived).
- Your target for early POC is to validate latency SLOs while hitting a target economics goal (~$ / 1M tokens range you mentioned on the call — need a concrete number).

What we need from you to run a meaningful simulation and recommend batching/concurrency config:
1) Monthly token range (min / expected / max) — ballpark is fine (e.g., 50M / 150M / 300M tokens).
2) Workload patterns: percent split (chat vs batch), avg user session concurrency (peak simultaneous active sessions), and traffic distribution (steady vs spiky).
3) Typical prompt + response average token lengths for each workload (chat: prompt avg, response avg; batch jobs: input avg, output avg).
4) Any strict latency SLOs (p95) or cost targets (target $ / 1M tokens).

Notes on Redwood assumptions we typically use for this type of workload:
- Continuous batching (short batching window, kernel-aware batching) gives biggest wins when there is prefix reuse (chat sessions). For streaming chat sessions we expect >2x unit cost improvement vs single-request policy once traffic passes ~10-20 reqs/sec per model backend.
- For bursty batch jobs we recommend transient Dedicated capacity or background EC2-backed pools to avoid latency penalties during synchronous serving.
- Concurrency guidance: plan for an initial config that supports 200–400 concurrent generation streams per model instance for chat-heavy workloads; we can tune down if your average tokens per request are small.

Next steps I propose:
- You share the ballpark numbers above and a sample anonymized traffic trace (CSV or Drive link).
- We run two simulations: Hosted cost estimate and Dedicated capacity estimate with batching/concurrency knobs.
- Schedule a short POC kickoff next week to lock measurement metrics.

Attaching a short requirements template (finlytics_poc_requirements.xlsx) and our latest pricing sheet for reference — I'll flag where batching assumptions materially change the unit economics.

Thanks,

Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0193

From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@finlytics.com>

Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: workload profile & batching / concurrency assumptions

Hi Ben — thanks for the clear list. See our initial answers below (happy to iterate):

1) Monthly token range (min / expected / max): 50,000,000 / 175,000,000 / 350,000,000 tokens.
2) Workload split & patterns:
   - Chat assistant: ~65% of requests, high session affinity (prefix reuse), sessions average 8 turns, largely US business hours with evening tail. Peak concurrency we see in internal benchmarks ~1,200 concurrent active users (peaks lasting ~5–10 minutes during batch notifications).
   - Summarization & analytics (batch): ~35%, scheduled windows overnight and some ad-hoc during business hours; these can be staged to avoid peak.
   - Traffic is moderately spiky (smoothing during peak hours; some weekend drops).
3) Avg token lengths:
   - Chat: user prompt avg 110 tokens, assistant response avg 320 tokens (includes system + history).
   - Batch jobs: input avg 2,500 tokens, output avg 1,100 tokens.
4) Latency SLOs & cost targets:
   - Chat: p95 generation latency target <= 600ms (we can accept partial streaming if needed).
   - Cost target: ideally $275 / 1M tokens or lower at scale (we understand tradeoffs).

Questions for you: how do cold sessions affect batching and unit economics (we expect many returning users but also a non-trivial cold-start rate)? Also curious how you'd model the overnight batch traffic in your cost sim (do you treat those as amortized cheaper tokens if scheduled).

I'll drop an anonymized, sampled traffic trace to the Drive folder you listed — formatting as timestamp, request_type, user_session_id, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens.

Best,
Emily Zhao
Head of ML Infrastructure | FinLytics, Inc.
emily.zhao@finlytics.com

--

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: workload profile & batching / concurrency assumptions

Emily — this is perfect, thanks. A few clarifications and how we'll proceed based on your numbers.

Cold sessions & batching:
- Cold sessions reduce prefix reuse, which in turn reduces batching efficiency. In practice we model cold-start fraction explicitly; if cold-starts are ~20–30% of chat traffic you still see sizable batching wins from the warm sessions. We'll ask for a short trace to estimate the working set and session reuse.

Modeling overnight batch jobs:
- For scheduled batch jobs we treat them as an opportunity to run on lower-cost Dedicated capacity (or preemptible pools) where latency is flexible. We amortize the GPU time and apply lower unit costs in the simulation (we'll show both Hosted and Dedicated options).

Initial cost/concurrency recommendations (POC baseline):
- Hosted POC (single-region, autoscaling): aim for target concurrency headroom = peak_concurrency * 1.2 = ~1440. We'll allocate model workers with continuous batching windows tuned to 15–30ms to favor streaming latency while still aggregating requests.
- Dedicated POC (if you want stricter p95s): start with 2x A100-equivalent GPU nodes configured for high-concurrency chat (we typically size ~250–300 active streams/GPU for this token profile). We'll run load-based tuning during POC.
- Expected unit cost: with your mix and target batching (assuming 75% effective prefix reuse on chat), we estimate a blended rate in the ballpark of $220–$320 / 1M tokens (we'll produce a precise sim). The biggest drivers: prefix reuse fraction, average completion length, and how much of the batch work you shift to lower-cost windows.

Next steps:
1) We'll ingest the sample trace you upload and run two sims (Hosted vs Dedicated).
2) I'll share a short deck and a pricing simulation by EOD Friday showing sensitivity to reuse and batch scheduling.
3) If the sim looks good, propose a 4-week POC: week 1 instrument + ingest traces, week 2 run realistic load tests, week 3 tune batching/concurrency, week 4 handoff + cost baseline.

Attaching our latest pricing sheet (redwood_pricing_sheet_v3.pdf) — see tab "Batching sensitivity" where we've parameterized reuse and average tokens.

Shall I schedule the kickoff for Monday morning PST? Marissa will be the RED lead on the engagement and Sergio will help on the SLA/pricing negotiation side.

Thanks — will prioritize the sim once we have the trace.
